events.title: St. John Vianney is sent to Ars
events.shortBlurb: A peasant's son who had failed his examinations was sent to a forgotten village and made it the confessional of France…
body: On 9 February 1818, a few weeks after the death of his mentor the Abbé Balley, the young priest Jean-Baptiste-Marie Vianney was appointed parish priest of Ars, a hamlet of some two hundred and thirty souls in the Dombes, north of Lyon, whose faith had grown cold since the Revolution.

Born at Dardilly in 1786 and ordained in 1815 after long struggles with Latin, he found the village so little known that, the story runs, he lost his way to it and was set right by a boy minding sheep. For more than forty years he prayed, fasted, preached against dancing and blasphemy, and reconciled sinners to God.

Ars became a place of pilgrimage: by the 1850s tens of thousands came every year, and the curé spent as many as sixteen hours a day in the confessional. He died in 1859, was canonized in 1925, and is the patron of parish priests throughout the world.
